PROJECT NO. 59142

REVIEW OF ERCOT’S § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES §
FOR LARGE LOADS § OF TEXAS

ORDER GRANTING GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTIONS

On August 3, 2026, Governor Greg Abbott issued a letter directing the Public Utility
Commission of Texas (Commission) and Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) to
conduct “a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s
interconnection process.”! The Governor further directed that this verification and audit be
completed before any additional data centers are approved to move forward. In response, ERCOT
intends to temporarily pause its transitional Batch Zero interconnection study of loads that are 75
MW or more (Large Loads), including data centers and virtual currency mining facilities, until the
verification and audit are complete.

On August 10, 2026, ERCOT filed with the Commission a request for good cause
exceptions, pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.3(b), to the requirement of 16
TAC § 25.361(b)(16), to allow ERCOT to deviate from ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 9.2.2(3)(a),
9.3.1(2)¢a), and 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii). ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) requires ERCOT to classify
Large Loads as base load, studied load, or load that has not met sufficient criteria to be included
in Batch Zero by August 7, 2026. During the pause of the Batch Zero study, ERCOT will verify
the accuracy of information Large Load developers submitted in support of their interconnection
requests. As part of the same effort, ERCOT will request the community impact information
identified in the Governor’s letter from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities of 25
MW or more that have not yet energized. The verification and audit will take several months, so
ERCOT was unable to meet an initial classification deadline in its rules for the Batch Zero study
process.

Given the delay in classifying Large Loads, ERCOT further requests an exception from the
requirement in ERCOT Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a){ii) that ERCOT include in the August 1 and

November 1, 2026 quarterly stability assessments (QSAs) only those Large Loads it has classified
as base load. ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1) provides that a Large Load will be classified
as base load if it qualifies for that designation under any one of the seven eligibility paths. Because
ERCOT now intends to delay its classification of Large Loads for several months to complete the
verification process required by the Governor’s letter, no Large Load will be able to meet the QSA
qualification requirement in Planning Guide § 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii) during this period. To avoid
unnecessary delay, ERCOT requests to allow those Large Loads that Interconnecting Distribution
Service Providers (DSPs) and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) submitted as base load and
that ERCOT has determined are eligible to qualify as base load but has not yet classified to be
included in the August 2026 and November 2026 QSAs.

ERCOT also requests authorization to allow it to continue to review dynamic data
submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline in ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.2(3)(a). ERCOT
was unable to review all the dynamic data submissions by the deadline due to internal processing
constraints and variations in how Interconnecting Large Load Entities (ILLEs) submitted their
data. ERCOT intends to complete its review of the remaining dynamic data submissions and notify
ILLEs of any deficiencies as soon as possible. ERCOT further requests ILLEs be permitted to
cure any deficiencies within 24 days of notification, which is the same cure period provided under
§ 9.2.2(3){a).

Good cause exists to allow ERCOT to complete the verification and audit and report the
results to the Commission before continuing the Batch Zero interconnection process. In
accordance with 16 TAC § 25.3(b), the Commission grants ERCOT a good cause exception from
the requirements of 16 TAC § 25.361(b)(16) that ERCOT (1) classify Large Loads by the August
7, 2026 deadline in accordance with ERCOT Planning Guide §§ 9.3.1(2)(a); and (2) include in the
August 1 and November 1, 2026 QSAs only those Large Loads that ERCOT has classified as base
load under ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1). The exceptions permit ERCOT to delay
classifying Large Loads for inclusion in Batch Zero and include in those QSAs Large Loads that
Interconnecting DSPs and TSPs submitted as base load and that ERCOT has determined are
eligible to qualify as base load but has not yet classified. Good cause also exists to allow ERCOT
to review dynamic data submissions after the August 7, 2026 deadline in ERCOT Planning Guide
§ 9.2.2(3)(a) and allow ILLEs to cure deficiencies within 24 days of notification.
